intro.title: SRE practices
intro.body: In this lesson, you will learn the foundational concepts of Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) by exploring key practices like Service Level Objectives (SLOs), error budgets, and incident management. You will simulate setting up SLOs and calculating error budgets to understand how to balance reliability with development velocity. The core concepts involve defining reliability targets, monitoring systems, and implementing automation for operational tasks. You'll work with constructs like SLO definitions, error budget calculations, and basic incident response workflows, all presented in a beginner-friendly, practical manner.
intro.usecase: SRE practices are implemented in production engineering through reliability dashboards that display service-level indicators like error rates and latency. These dashboards help teams monitor system health in real-time, such as tracking API performance or database uptime across distributed services. Engineers use SRE principles to set error budgets and automate incident response, ensuring high availability for user-facing products like e-commerce platforms or streaming services. This approach enables proactive maintenance and rapid recovery from outages, maintaining consistent user experience under varying loads.
